data.body:
Scope input from bug 55bc (rebar-debug), which removed the automatic prune from the three LLM sidecar emit paths for the same reason. Measurements from THIS repo's live tracker, plus an experiment that changes the design space.

## Measured today (rebar's own tickets branch, 49,598 commits)

- REVIEW_RESULT: 3,207 files, 118 MB on disk. Mean 36.0 KB/event, median 32.5 KB, max 144 KB.
- COMPLETION_VERDICT: 444 files, 1.76 MB (mean ~4 KB).
- All event files: 15,548 files, 251 MB. So REVIEW_RESULT alone is ~47%% of the working tree.
- Packed .git: 1.02 GiB.
- Distribution is extremely skewed: 1,238 tickets have >=1 REVIEW_RESULT, but the MEDIAN is 1 and the mean 2.6. Only 3 tickets ever reached the 50 cap; only 20 exceed 10.
- Prune history: 6,844 sidecar events ever added, 3,200 ever deleted, across 2,473 prune commits - but concentrated in just 55 tickets (~58 deletions each). Retention is inert for ~96%% of tickets and very active on a few hot, repeatedly-re-reviewed ones.
- Current rate: 5,906 REVIEW_RESULT added in 2026-07 alone (~200 MB/month of working tree at 36 KB each).

## The part that reframes the tradeoff

Deleting a committed file does NOT reclaim repository space - the blob stays in history forever. The 1.02 GiB pack already contains all 6,844 sidecar blobs regardless of the 3,200 deletions. So physical prune never reduced clone/fetch cost; it only reduced CHECKOUT size, while ADDING 2,473 commits (plus their tree objects) and breaking cross-clone merges. As a size measure on an append-only git store it is close to all cost and no benefit.

Implication for this ticket: the dominant lever is PAYLOAD SIZE, not event count. 36 KB mean per REVIEW_RESULT is the real driver; cutting it to ~4 KB is a ~9x win that requires no deletion and no merge semantics change at all.

## Experiment: rename detection is the actual conflict mechanism, and it is configurable

The wedge is not caused by deletion per se. It is caused by git RENAME DETECTION pairing the shared deleted file against each clone's distinct new file (CONFLICT rename/rename). Verified: with the automatic prune RESTORED at all three sidecar sites but 'merge.renames = false' set on both clones' trackers, the two-clone union merge SUCCEEDS at all three sites (3/3 pass) where it previously conflicted 3/3.

That is a genuinely merge-safe route to keeping retention. In a UUID-named append-only store a 'rename' is never real, so disabling rename detection is arguably the correct configuration independent of retention. It would need: init writing the config on tracker creation (it already writes commit.gpgsign there), an ensure-registry migration for existing clones, and a decision on whether deleting committed events is acceptable at all given docs/concurrency.md invariant I1 - which currently says it is not. Reinstating deletion would require amending I1 deliberately, not incidentally.
